lecture: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table
title: Inside the atom
brief: A textbook atom diagram labels the tiny nucleus, its protons and neutrons, and electrons arranged on surrounding shells.

title: The atomic structure
brief: A labelled atom map shows a small positively charged nucleus at the centre, negative electrons on circular or elliptical orbits, and the surrounding mostly empty space.

title: Evidence from alpha scattering
brief: An alpha-scattering atom map tracks alpha particles from the foil to three outcomes—straight through, small deflection and large or backward deflection—and links each observation to the nucleus conclusion.

lecture: Relative masses of atoms and molecules
title: What relative atomic mass means
brief: An atom-count map contrasts carbon-12's twelve-part reference with chlorine isotope masses, leading to Ar(Cl) = 35.5 without a unit.

title: Formulae from particle models
brief: An atom-count map isolates one methane particle, converts its one carbon and four hydrogen atoms into CH₄, and checks the counts. Picture: one methane particle with one carbon atom joined to four hydrogen atoms.

lecture: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table
title: Filling electron shells
brief: A shell-filling calculation distributes calcium’s 20 electrons across capacities 2, 8, 8 and 2, then applies the same rule to phosphorus.

title: Electron transfer in sodium chloride
brief: A dot-and-cross electron map follows sodium and chlorine from their outer shells to bracketed Na+ and Cl− ions, with the transferred electron visibly tracked.

title: Forming magnesium oxide
brief: A two-electron transfer map tracks magnesium crosses into oxygen, producing bracketed Mg2+ and O2− ions and the balanced formula MgO.

title: Molten ionic compounds
brief: A labelled molten lead(II) bromide cell shows the power supply, positive anode, negative cathode, ions, equations, and visible products.

title: Meaning and parts of an electrolytic cell
brief: A labelled electrolytic cell is built from the direct-current supply, electrolyte, anode, cathode, and connecting wires.

title: Aqueous copper(II) sulfate
brief: Two atom maps compare carbon and copper electrodes, tracking copper ions, copper transfer, oxygen formation, solution colour, and separate electrical energy.

title: VSEPR shapes and angles
brief: A rotatable VSEPR set compares linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal pyramidal, and bent structures while lone pairs explain reduced bond angles.

title: Hybridization and valence bond theory
brief: Orbital-mixing pathways connect sp, sp2, and sp3 hybridization to electron-domain arrangements, while overlapping orbitals form sigma bonds.

lecture: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table
title: Groups, periods and noble gases
brief: A periodic-table relationship scene maps outer electrons to group, occupied shells to period, and full outer shells to noble gases.

title: Why crack crude oil fractions?
brief: A refinery flow compares heavy, low-demand fractions with smaller alkane fuels and alkene feedstocks, while the decane equation checks both atom totals.

title: Making alkanes
brief: A reaction pathway contrasts hydrogenation and cracking, labels reagents and conditions, and checks atom conservation in the worked hydrogenation.
